title: Architectural machine state
statement: A machine state is an explicit tuple of architectural components: word-valued registers, byte-addressed memory, a program counter, named condition state, and a normal-or-trapped outcome. A particular theorem may use a declared projection of this tuple, but it may not hide a component that its instructions read or write.

formal.statement: State w := Registers w × Memory × ProgramCounter w × Conditions × Outcome

notes: Book-level foundation. Axeyum has bit-vector terms but no reusable architectural-state library at this audit.
